propositions: A closed child with disposition class (duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated) and a live replacement link is exempted from completion verification by the close path but incorrectly treated as uncertified by the certification path, blocking the parent's signature

The close gate and certification path implement conflicting rules on the same exemption, creating a state with no non-force exit: the child cannot earn an attestation, --force-close produces exactly the uncertified state the operator ruling prohibits, and all workarounds require misrepresenting the tree

Disposition-closed duplicates without a declared replacement link are currently certifiable, while those with an honest link are unsigned, creating an inversion where better documentation causes lost certification

The _completion_precheck docstring does not document its disposition branch, causing callers like child_closure_findings to treat unsigned closures as always uncertified rather than recognizing the exemption
Per operator ruling, disposition closes must provide attestation (with DISPOSITION marker, not PASS claim) and resolution through the replacement link rather than withholding certification
The --force-close guard must execute before the disposition branch to prevent force-close from bypassing verification on linked duplicates
